facts.raw_span: A 67-year-old woman
31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder
depressed mood, anhedonia, nervousness, fatigue, decreased appetite, and poor sleep
beginning 5 months after COVID-19
two severe episodes responsive to escitalopram (up to 20 mg/d) and duloxetine (up to 60 mg/d)
intolerance to venlafaxine, bupropion, and trazodone
mother had mania
denied iron deficiency anemia, hypothyroidism, or substance abuse
Physical and neurologic examinations and routine laboratory tests were unremarkable
new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms
worse at rest, partially relieved by movement, and predominantly occurring in the evening
causing night-time sleep disturbance

concepts.why: The patient has a 31-year history of recurrent depressive disorder with symptoms of depressed mood, anhedonia, and fatigue, which are characteristic of Major Depressive Disorder.
The patient's new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms, worse at rest and partially relieved by movement, are consistent with Restless Legs Syndrome.
The patient's depressive episode began 5 months after COVID-19, suggesting a possible link between the two, which is consistent with Post-COVID-19 Depression.
The patient's mother had mania, which increases the patient's risk of developing Bipolar Disorder, although the patient's symptoms are currently more consistent with Major Depressive Disorder.
The patient's new deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms, which began while she was taking duloxetine, may be related to duloxetine-induced akathisia.
The patient's new symptoms began after escitalopram was discontinued, which may be related to escitalopram withdrawal.

The patient's new symptoms, including deep itching and creeping sensations, may be related to serotonin syndrome, although the patient's medication regimen and symptoms do not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

The patient's deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms may be related to neuropathic pain, although the patient's symptoms and medication regimen do not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

The patient's symptoms of nervousness and intolerance to certain medications may be related to an anxiety disorder, although the patient's symptoms are currently more consistent with Major Depressive Disorder.

The patient's new symptoms, including deep itching and creeping sensations, may be related to a medication-induced movement disorder, although the patient's medication regimen and symptoms do not strongly suggest this diagnosis.

rationales.F04: The onset of symptoms 5 months after COVID-19 supports the diagnosis of Post-COVID-19 Depression.
rationales.F07: The patient's family history of mania supports the diagnosis of Bipolar Disorder.
rationales.F10: The patient's symptoms of deep itching and creeping sensations in her bilateral shoulders and arms are consistent with Restless Legs Syndrome and Duloxetine-Induced Akathisia.
rationales.F11: The patient's symptoms worsening at rest and improving with movement are consistent with Restless Legs Syndrome and Duloxetine-Induced Akathisia.
